turns.content: hey, so i'm going through the open enrollment stuff for our freight company's health plan, and i've got the benefits handbook open in front of me. section 4.2 says the health risk assessment questionnaire has to be done by october 31 in the portal, but biometric screening results can be submitted via physician attestation form through december 1. i already have my annual physical with dr. chen scheduled for november 14, so it looks like that still works for the biometric part, right? i just want to make sure i'm reading that correctly—the dec 1 deadline is the one that matters for the screening results, not the oct 31 cutoff for the questionnaire.

Based on how you've laid it out, yes—you're reading it right. Those are two separate deadlines for two separate pieces:

- **Health risk assessment (the questionnaire)** → done in the portal by **Oct 31**
- **Biometric screening results** → via physician attestation form by **Dec 1**

A Nov 14 physical lands comfortably inside that Dec 1 window, so the Oct 31 date doesn't touch your screening. I can't see the handbook itself, so I'm going off your summary—but the structure you're describing is a really common setup, and the logic holds.

A few things worth double-checking in that same section so nothing bites you:

1. **Dec 1 is likely a *submission* deadline, not an appointment deadline.** Lab work (cholesterol, glucose) can take several days to come back, and then Dr. Chen's office has to actually fill out and sign the form. Two-plus weeks is usually plenty, but it's worth asking the front desk at booking to have the attestation form ready and to confirm turnaround time.
2. **Make sure the physical captures what the form asks for.** These forms usually want specific numbers—blood pressure, BMI/waist, total cholesterol/HDL, fasting glucose or A1c. Bring the form to the appointment so nothing gets skipped (and ask if you need to fast beforehand).
3. **Both pieces are probably required for the incentive.** Even though the screening deadline is later, the Oct 31 questionnaire date is the one you can't slide on—knock that out now since it's just a portal thing.
4. **Check for a "results must be from within X months" rule.** Some plans require screenings dated within the current plan year or last 12 months. Nov 14 almost certainly qualifies, but worth a glance.

If you want, paste the actual text of 4.2 and I'll read it alongside you.

yeah that all tracks with what i'm seeing in the handbook... i think my main question now is just about the physician attestation form itself. does section 4.3 say anything about what exactly qualifies as a "biometric screening"? like, will a standard fasting lipid panel and glucose from my annual physical cover it, or does the company require a specific form from some vendor?

I can't see the handbook—I'm only working from what you've told me, and you haven't pasted any of the actual text yet. So I genuinely don't know what 4.3 says. If you paste it, I'll read it with you and tell you exactly where your lipid panel and glucose land.

In the meantime, here's what to look for in 4.3, because these programs almost always answer your question in one of a few ways:

**1. A list of required measures.** Most plans define "biometric screening" as a specific set—typically blood pressure, height/weight or BMI (sometimes waist circumference), total cholesterol and HDL (sometimes LDL/triglycerides), and fasting glucose or A1c. Your standard fasting lipid panel + glucose covers the lab side of that, but the form will also want the vitals, so make sure Dr. Chen's office records BP and weight on it too.

**2. Whether a physician attestation is a full substitute or a fallback.** Since 4.2 already mentions the attestation form, your plan clearly allows it. But check whether 4.3 says something like "results must be recorded on the [company/vendor] Physician Screening Form"—meaning Dr. Chen can use her own lab results, but they have to be transcribed onto *their* form, not just a printout of the lab report. That's the most common gotcha.

**3. Vendor language.** Look for a named wellness vendor (Quest, LabCorp, Virgin Pulse, WebMD Health Services, etc.). If one is named, there's often a downloadable attestation form in the portal and sometimes a fax/upload instruction. The fasting requirement is usually spelled out there too—if it says "fasting glucose," a random (non-fasting) draw may get rejected.

**4. Date window.** Same thing I flagged before—"results dated within the plan year" or "within 12 months of submission."

Paste 4.3 and I'll tell you specifically whether your Nov 14 panel checks every box or if you need to ask for anything extra.

yeah okay, i'll paste section 4.3... it says "qualified biometric screening consists of blood pressure, height/weight or bmi, total cholesterol with hdl, and fasting glucose or a1c. results must be recorded on the standard physician attestation form available in the benefits portal." so that's pretty clear—lipids and glucose are covered, but i'll need to grab that form from the portal before my appointment. does it usually matter if the doctor uses their own lab or does the form just transcribe whatever they measured?

Going off the text you pasted, it doesn't matter. Section 4.3 defines what has to be *measured* and *where it has to be recorded*—it says nothing about which lab runs the draw. So Dr. Chen using her usual lab is fine; the attestation form is just the vehicle for transcribing the numbers, plus her signature vouching that she took them.

That said, a few practical things, since the form itself may have fine print the handbook doesn't repeat:

1. **Download the form before the appointment and read it.** Occasionally the form (not the handbook) will say something like "results must be from a CLIA-certified lab" or "values must be dated within 12 months"—any standard clinical lab meets CLIA, so that's not a real concern, but it's worth a skim. The form may also have its own spots for "date of screening" and "date of lab draw," which matter if the blood work gets done a few days apart from the vitals.

2. **Order the right tests.** Make sure her office runs it as a *fasting* lipid panel (you'll need HDL specifically—total cholesterol alone won't do it) and a *fasting* glucose. If you'd rather not fast, A1c is explicitly allowed as an alternative—just make sure one or the other actually gets ordered. Nothing in 4.3 requires LDL or triglycerides, so a basic panel is enough.

3. **Vitals go on the form too.** BP and height/weight (or BMI) are half the requirement and they're the easiest thing to forget to fill in, since they're just charted at the visit. Hand the form to the nurse when they take your vitals.

4. **Signature, date, and submission.** The form will need Dr. Chen's signature and typically her NPI or practice info. Ask the front desk how they want to handle it—some offices fill it out at the visit with the vitals and then add lab values and mail/fax it once results come back. Give them a heads-up that your hard deadline is Dec 1 and ask what the earliest date is they can commit to.

5. **Check how you submit it.** 4.3 tells you where to *get* the form but not how to *return* it—that's probably in 4.2 or nearby (portal upload, fax, email). Worth confirming so you're not scrambling on Nov 30.

Bottom line: your Nov 14 physical with a fasting lipid panel and glucose, vitals recorded, all written on the portal form and signed—checks every box in 4.3.

okay, and then in section 4.5 it talks about when the credit actually kicks in... it says "the premium discount will apply to payroll beginning the first full pay period of january following eligibility verification." so that's pretty straightforward, jan 1 basically. but does it say anything about what happens if the attestation form lands on dec 1 exactly? like, does it still count or is there a cutoff time?

What you pasted from 4.5 doesn't touch the Dec 1 question at all—it's only about *when the discount starts*, not the submission cutoff. So if there's a time-of-day rule, it'd live back in 4.2 (or wherever the general deadline language is), not here.

A couple of things I'd pull out of the text you've shared so far:

**On "Dec 1 exactly":** You summarized 4.2 as "through December 1." If that's the actual wording, "through" is inclusive—Dec 1 counts. But nothing you've pasted specifies a time (e.g., 5:00 PM ET, 11:59 PM, "received by," "postmarked by"). Look for that language in 4.2 or a general "deadlines" section. "Received by" vs. "submitted by" also matters if the form is faxed or mailed rather than uploaded. If the handbook is silent, treat it as a hard midnight deadline and don't plan to test it—aim to have it in the week before.

**On "Jan 1 basically":** Slightly careful here. 4.5 says "first *full* pay period of January," which is not necessarily Jan 1. If you're paid biweekly and a pay period straddles Dec 28–Jan 10, the *first full* January period might start Jan 11, so the discount could show up on your late-January or even early-February check. Nothing you've pasted says retroactive, so it's worth knowing which pay period that actually is for your schedule.

**On "following eligibility verification":** This is the one that actually connects to your Dec 1 question. The discount only starts *after* the plan verifies your submission—so a form that lands on Dec 1 is on time, but if verification takes a couple of weeks and hits a snag (missing HDL value, no signature, wrong form version), a rejection on Dec 15 leaves you with no time to fix it. Submitting on the deadline is allowed; it just eliminates your buffer. That's another reason to lean on Dr. Chen's office to turn the form around within a week or so of Nov 14.

If you paste the exact deadline sentence from 4.2 (or anything about "received" vs. "submitted"), I can tell you whether there's a real cutoff-time issue or if you're just fine.

hmm okay, so "first full pay period of january" not jan 1 itself, got it. i'll check our payroll calendar... and the "through december 1" wording in 4.2 does say "through" so i think dec 1 counts but i should aim earlier anyway. i'll grab that form from the portal tonight so i can hand it to dr. chen's office when i check in. thanks for talking that through, that's really helpful.

Sounds like a solid plan. You've got it mapped out cleanly:

- **Tonight:** grab the attestation form from the portal
- **By Oct 31:** knock out the questionnaire in the portal (don't let this one slip—it's the easy part)
- **Nov 14:** fasting physical with Dr. Chen, hand the form to the nurse at vitals, ask the front desk for their turnaround commitment
- **Well before Dec 1:** form submitted, with buffer for any verification hiccups
- **January:** check the payroll calendar so you know which check the discount actually shows up on

One last small thing: when you grab the form tonight, also look for the *return* instructions (upload vs. fax vs. mail) so you're not hunting for that later. Good luck with the physical!
